prospect.name: Travis Owen
prospect.location: Solana Beach, San Diego County, California, USA. Raised partly on Vancouver Island near Victoria and on a ranch near Innisfail, Alberta.
prospect.occupation: Retired. Career in sales — pagers, cell phones and phone systems — then mortgage and real estate broking, then co-founded a phone company he sold roughly fourteen years later, then twelve years in the cannabis business from around 2008, which paid off a commercial warehouse in East County San Diego. Owns several California properties, all paid off, and lives on retirement income plus rent from the commercial property.
prospect.family_status: Recently single after a divorce and dating actively. Two daughters aged 29 and 25; the elder marries in October and they take weekly private ballroom dance lessons together to prepare for the father-daughter dance. One daughter lives with his ex-wife.
prospect.training_background: Lifelong exerciser. Former college soccer player, former weightlifter, trained Brazilian jiu-jitsu for many years, plus skiing, tennis and soccer. Currently hot yoga around eight times a month, daily walking with a 10,000-step target, push-ups and some kettlebell work. Owns two 20 kg kettlebells and bought a rack a few weeks ago. Follows Trevor plus three or four other coaches and copies individual movements without a structured programme — 'I'll go like eight minutes. And then I finally start falling off, check my phone.' Cannot sprint or play basketball because of the hip replacements.
prospect.medical: Substantial. Two total hip replacements — the first at 45 or 46, that one revised about eight years ago, and then the other side — which he attributes to jiu-jitsu, skiing, tennis and soccer; he cannot sprint or run. AC joint surgeries on the shoulders, which he reports as now pain-free and fully mobile. Shortened Achilles tendons that hot yoga has not lengthened. Total cholesterol peaked at 240 four months ago, since reduced to 183; high triglycerides; calcium score of zero. Declined statins and explicitly refuses them — 'once you're on those, you're kind of like on them for life.' Currently six to eight weeks into low-dose tirzepatide, which he intends to stop after a month, and had to insist his provider run monthly bloods. History of kidney stones twice, a fatty gallbladder and unexplained abdominal pain investigated by hospital scans, which he attributes to years of poor nutrition. Struggles with sleep. Describes night eating as an addiction and an emotional habit.

signals: Lost ground across a hard season and names it as self-inflicted with explicit regret: 'it really is all self-induced, and I now see it, like, I can look from above and be like, you did that to yourself, you chose that life'

A specific triggering event four months ago: 'I had high lipids, high cholesterol, and I got really upset at myself. I was like, what am I doing, dude? My cholesterol was 240... And I said, this is not acceptable.'
Wants a former self back — college soccer player and weightlifter, now 20 to 30 lb heavier than his best and chasing 'I want to be lean. I want to be jacked'
Mortality is explicit and near the surface: 'we're in the death zone as we move into our 60s' and 'I'm in the final quarter'

Not the_preserver despite the age and the health literacy: the preserver's defining goal is holding on to function rather than gaining, and this prospect is unambiguously chasing gain — 10 to 12% body fat, 'top 1% for 63-year-olds', and a visible physique
Genuine preserver overlap in behaviour though — monthly blood panels, monthly body composition scans, a Hume band, a calcium score, and a considered refusal of statins

goals.text: Get lean and 'jacked for my age' — down from around 19% body fat to 10 or 12%
Reduce visceral fat specifically, which he links to cancer and disease risk
Stay healthy, mobile and disease-free for the next twenty years, into his eighties
A structured nutrition format he can follow without the tirzepatide — his single most repeated ask
Make it a permanent life choice rather than a two-month push
Structure and discipline, which he ties directly to avoiding bad decisions and toxic relationships
Be a visible example to his two adult daughters, who are starting to walk and dance with him
Attract a better partner — dating is an explicit and repeated driver
Travel and walk European towns rather than ride a tour bus
Functional strength rather than the ego-driven size he trained for in the eighties
Better sleep and mental health, which he frames as inseparable from physical health

pains.text: No format for either nutrition or training — 'I don't have a format for my nutrition, I don't have really a format for my exercise, and I feel nutrition is such a large component'
Night eating he describes as an addiction and an emotional coping habit left over from years as a stressed sole provider
Cannot sustain a session — starts strong, fades at eight minutes, checks his phone
Dependent for now on tirzepatide to control the night eating and fears losing the results when he stops
Cholesterol reached 240 four months ago and he refuses statins, leaving lifestyle as his only lever
Two hip replacements that rule out running, sprinting and basketball
Shortened Achilles tendons that yoga has not improved
Isolation — describes himself as a loner without a larger group, and says doing it alone is the hard part
Sustained frustration and demoralisation with dating, raised repeatedly and at length
Not as educated as a coach and knows it — 'You don't always make the right choices because you're not as educated as you guys are'

objections.rep_response: Not addressed. The rep had just confirmed, when pressed, that the live coaching calls are group rather than individual, which is the substance of this concern, and moved straight to the trial offer instead of answering it.

offer.payment_plan_terms: Initially denied in substance — asked directly whether payment plans exist, the rep answered 'most people just put it on a credit card and pay it all at once' and then 'majority of people just put it on the credit card and go from there.' Roughly ten minutes later he disclosed that plans do exist: 'we do usually have a few options to break it up. If we are breaking it up, usually we'll charge a little bit of interest in terms of, you know, there's an extra couple hundred bucks each payment just because we're breaking it up rather than doing it all up front.' No term, instalment count or total was stated. The $1,200 love-it-or-leave-it was explained correctly as crediting toward the $6,000 with $4,800 remaining.

prospect_financials.note: Volunteered, not elicited. 'I live off of seven to nine grand a month' from retirement income plus rent on a paid-off commercial warehouse, and the $6,000 would come out of savings — 'that's out of my savings.' Owns several California properties outright. No financial-picture question was asked at any point.

evidence: No payment and no link. The prospect declined a same-day decision: 'it is something that I am going to contemplate and think about for a minute. I'm not just going to be like, here's my credit card this moment.'

The rep tested for an immediate close and read the room accurately: 'it is sounding like that's not, we're not, I'm kind of getting the sense that we're still not feeling good 100%. Let's rock and roll with that right now.'

Counter-evidence, strongly positive: he named the tier he intends to take and wrote the figure down — 'I really am leaning towards doing this actually, but the love it or leave it. And I'm writing this down to $1,200. That is the direction that I would want to go.'
Counter-evidence, positive: rated the programme eight to nine out of ten twice and said 'I like you. I like Trevor. I got the price. I got the formula.'

Counter-evidence, negative: the reason for the eight rather than ten was never resolved — 'until I'm doing it, I can't give the 10... right now, it's like, the girl looks like an eight, but man, until you open up the package, you don't know.'

No follow-up call was booked. The arrangement is that the prospect has the rep's personal number and they will text, with an outstanding personal favour attached — the prospect asked for and was promised accommodation contacts in Medellín.
outcome.next_step: Informal text follow-up, no date and no calendar hold. The prospect has stated the $1,200 love-it-or-leave-it is the route he wants. He has monthly blood work arriving and a body-composition scan booked for the following week that he intends to use as a baseline.

notable.note: The most medically complex prospect in the batch received the thinnest baseline in the batch. Two hip replacements, one of them revised, plus AC joint surgeries and shortened Achilles tendons, plus active low-dose tirzepatide use he intends to stop, plus a cholesterol scare four months ago and a stated refusal of statins — and the rep asked one health question, said 'Okay', and never asked about diet, sleep, energy, injuries or limitations at all. When the prospect raised his shortened Achilles and asked a direct programming question about a ramp board, he was told to take it up with Trevor, who 'has been thousands and thousands of people with pretty much every different health condition, injury, limitation you can buy.' The rep also relayed a position on the prospect's prescription medication: 'Trevor's opinion is that you don't need it.' Commercially, this is the third call in the batch where a prospect asked directly about payment plans and was told most people pay upfront — and the only one where the rep then contradicted himself ten minutes later by disclosing that plans exist with a surcharge of 'an extra couple hundred bucks each payment'. Two further points a manager should see: the call opened with the rep noticing it was being live streamed and turning that off, with no recording disclosure to the prospect at any point; and about five minutes of the call were spent on the prospect's dating frustrations, ending with the rep offering to arrange accommodation contacts for him in Medellín, which the prospect then referenced as something he wanted alongside the purchase.

quality.notes: Continuous inversion throughout, and unusually bad in the long monologue sections. Whole rep passages sit under Travis Owen's label — the three-pillar delivery, the janitor analogy, the plane metaphor and the $1,200 offer are all mislabelled at various points — and several turns fuse both speakers with no break, notably the extended dating tangent around 00:29:30 where four alternating turns run together. The $6,000 quote and the payment-plan exchange were attributed by content. The prospect is far more talkative than the rep, which makes label-based attribution particularly unreliable here.
